column1: # boru Language Specification: CODE BODIES and quoted operands
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Family: code-bodies. The construct family that declines most in REAL
# code: `do` bodies; `if` / `case` / `guard` / `var` / `while` / `for`
# bodies; bodies bound to a `def` and driven later; bodies parked in a
# map, a list or a flex store and fetched at run time; bodies over
# COMPUTED collections; bodies that define locals; bodies that read an
# enclosing binding; bodies that MUTATE an enclosing binding from inside
# a loop; a code body arriving as a function PARAMETER; quoted lists
# evaluated later; and the macro-ish / quoted-operand shapes (`quote`,
# `unquote`, `splice`, `macro`, `behave`, query clause lists).
# EVERY row's expected column is the value the INTERPRETER produces,
# measured — never guessed. Each input was run as
#   boru do -no-compile '<input> end <drops> canon end print end <drops>'
# once per residual slot, so the expected column is literally
# `core.Canon(stack)`, the string test/specfix compares against. The
# capture method was validated against 380 existing rows (control,
# codequote, list, higher-order, macro, each-variants, callbacks) before
# a single row here was written; it reproduced all 380 exactly.
# ROWS THAT FAIL TO COMPILE TO COMPILE ARE RECORDED DELIBERATELY, AS OPEN
# DEFECTS. Each such row was then run under `BORU_FORCE_COMPILE=1` and
# its description carries the compile failure VERBATIM, so the reason text is
# the ledger of what is left to build. They are not mistakes and must
# not be deleted to make a ceiling green. The compiler scores ~96% on
# the old one-liner corpus and ~65% on real files precisely because a
# compile failure is WHOLE-PROGRAM and latches on the FIRST unsupported
# construct, and the old corpus never COMBINED constructs. Combining
# them is what this file does.
# Two rows are marked `DOES NOT COMPILE: HARD ERROR` rather than a compile failure:
# under BORU_FORCE_COMPILE=1 they do not decline the program, they
# ABORT it — an internal_error or a case_error the interpreter never
# raises. Those are the sharpest defects in the file.
# NOTE FOR THE RATCHET: test/go/langspec/compiled_coverage_test.go holds
# failureCeiling = 0. The declining rows below are NEW EVIDENCE, not
# regressions — the ceiling must be re-based (as it must for
# callbacks.tsv and each-variants.tsv, written in the same corpus
# expansion), or this file moved under a documented tier.
# Two known defects found while writing this file are DELIBERATELY NOT
# recorded as rows, because they would fail hard gates rather than a
# ratchet, and a red differential gate hides everything else:
#   1. SILENT WRONG ANSWER (fails TestSpecCompiledDifferential):
#        def t 0 end for 3 [each [def t (t add 1) t] [0] drop] end t
#      interpreter -> 3, bytecode -> 0. An `each` body's `def` of an
#      enclosing binding is LOST when the each sits inside a `for` body.
#      Compare the row in section 9 with the `do` wrapper, which declines
#      cleanly, and the bare `for 3 [def t (t add 1)]`, which is correct.
#   2. NON-TERMINATION (fails everything, slowly):
#        def t 0 end while [t lt 3] [each [def t (t add 1) t] [0] drop] end t
#      interpreter -> 3; under BORU_FORCE_COMPILE=1 the same program
#      spins to the 10,000,000-step evaluation limit. Same lost `def`
#      as (1), but now the loop's own exit condition depends on it.
# See also: each-variants.tsv (the `each` family), callbacks.tsv (fn
# values travelling as data), control.tsv (the one-liner baseline).
